description: Third independent scenario for C-append-log-identity-consistency, testing the vote-facing consequence opened by the claim. After the truncation-then-failure premise, the node's real log ends at index 1 term 1 while its cached last entry still reads index 3 term 2, so a RequestVote from a candidate whose log ends at index 2 term 2 is strictly more up to date than the real log and must be granted. The oracle is the vote handler's own Granted field (granted == true); identity is the single node the history belongs to.

harness.description: In-package Go test that drives the confirmed truncation-then-StoreLogs-failure premise, then calls the real requestVote handler with a candidate whose log is more up to date than the node's real log, reporting the cached and real identities and the granted result.
semantic_changes: skipStartup is set so the main goroutine does not run; appendEntries and requestVote are driven directly with real RPC structs.
The store wrapper fails exactly one StoreLogs call to produce the stale cached identity, and no other store behaviour is changed.

legality.derivation: The premise is the accepted first scenario: a follower truncates a conflicting suffix and then its StoreLogs fails, leaving the cached last log identity ahead of the store. A RequestVote at the next term is then a legal input: the candidate is a voter-side request the node would answer on any path, and its log position is chosen to be strictly more up to date than the node's real log, so the up-to-date rule requires a grant.
legality.applicability: The node is Follower with the stale cached identity left by the failed append; the vote request carries the node's current term and a leader address. The proposition is local to this node.
unresolved: Whether the withheld vote can change an election outcome in a legal configuration.
alternatives: A candidate less up to date than the phantom but not the real log would also be plausible to refuse; this scenario uses a candidate strictly above the real log to isolate the cache as the cause.

grounding.derivation: The vote handler compares the candidate's LastLogTerm/LastLogIndex with r.getLastEntry(), which reads the cached identity, so a cache ahead of the store can refuse a candidate the real log does not justify refusing. The handler's own Granted field is the discriminator.
grounding.applicability: Admitted only for the node that experienced the truncation failure, correlated by the node label shared between the prerequisite and the result event.
alternatives: The request could be refused for 1another reason - term, configuration or an existing vote; the harness uses the node's current term, an empty configuration and no prior vote, so only the up-to-date comparison remains.

observable_properties.description: A node whose cached last log identity is ahead of its real log must still grant a vote to a candidate more up to date than that real log; the compared field is the vote handler's own Granted result.

uncertainties: The check establishes the local vote-withholding effect, not an election outcome; it uses an artificial single StoreLogs failure.
Only the cached-identity cause is exercised; other vote-path conditions are held fixed.
